incident-bot: INCIDENT: Elevated p95 token latency on serving-cluster-us-east-1 (auto-alert). Severity: S2. Paging on-call rotation.
incident-bot: Alerts: [p95_tokens > 450ms for 5m], error-rate spiked for model-redwood-alpha.
rita: paging @sam (on-call) — seeing large tail latency with continuous-batching enabled last deploy. p95 ~ 680ms, throughput still OK but several customers seeing slow responses.
sam: on it. pulling traces. @devon can you drop into the runtime dash? looks like batching window has ballooned.
devon: on dashboard — batch_size_distribution shifted right, mean_batch_size 48 (normally ~12). The batching window parameter "continuous_batch_target_ms" seems to be up to 250ms in recent config change.
nina: which rollout changed it? I see a config push from staging->prod yesterday by infra-auto-apply.
sam: ok immediate mitigation options: 1) reduce continuous_batch_target_ms to 50ms 2) throttle low-priority routes to reduce batch coalescing 3) temporarily flip to per-request (disable continuous batching) for the alpha model.
sam: priority order: 2 + 1 first to avoid full disable. I'll apply rate limiting to free-tier routes (10rps per key) and decrease continuous target to 60ms.
devon: agree. note: reducing target_ms will raise CPU/GPU overhead per token — cost increase acceptable short-term.
nina: i'll prepare a quota override for impacted enterprise customers if we need to extend limits. ping if that becomes necessary.
sam: executing mitigation: 
```
# reduce continuous batching target
redwoodctl config set serving.continuous_batch_target_ms=60 --cluster=us-east-1 --model=redwood-alpha
# apply soft rate limits for free-tier
redwoodctl routing set-rate-limit --route=/v1/generate --tier=free --limit=10rps --cluster=us-east-1
```
ops-runner-bot: runbook note: Changed continuous_batch_target_ms from 250 -> 60 on serving-cluster-us-east-1 for redwood-alpha. Applied soft rate limits to /v1/generate free tier.
sam: watching metrics now. p95 dropping from 680ms -> 290ms within 40s. successful requests per min dipped ~12% for free tier.
devon: batch_size_distribution now mean ~14, tail trimmed. p50 stable.
rita: customer impact: only free-tier customers saw degraded throughput; enterprise SLAs unaffected. I opened support ticket for top-5 affected orgs and flagged for quota temporary credits if they complain.
nina: good, but some high-cost internal tests saw error 429s. make sure we propagate the quota override for internal perf harness.
sam: noted. will add adhoc override for internal keys.
devon: small regressions in token-per-second efficiency observed but latency SLOs preserved.
sam: proposing revert plan: once p95 < 250ms for 10m and error-rate back to baseline, we roll continuous_batch_target_ms to 120ms and relax free-tier limits to 25rps to balance cost/latency.
rita: if any enterprise requests rollback, escalate to eng-runtime lead.
nina: I'll coordinate customer comms and update status page: "Mitigation applied: reduced batching window and limited low-priority routes; service degraded for small subset of users; now stabilizing."
sam: hitting +1 on that message. handing off to @devon for next 30m watch. I'm logging the incident and will create a postmortem if we see recurrence.
ops-runner-bot: oncall handoff: sam -> devon at 2301234780.
devon: will monitor. leaving lightweight sampling traces on high-variance batches. If p95 climbs back >400ms, we consider disabling continuous batching for alpha for 10m and routing to warm model-variant with smaller KV cache.
sam: thanks team. updating thread with metric links: https://observability.example.com/redwood-alpha/us-east-1?range=15m
rita: thanks. added to incident tracker. closing page once stable for 20m. :white_check_mark:
ops-runner-bot: incident marked: mitigation_applied.
